value.body: Fabric sourcing executives find the right fabrics and trims for garment and home-textile orders, at the right price and on time. They work with export houses, buying offices, brands and retailers. The day involves supplier calls, sample checks, price negotiation and tracking deliveries against production plans.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / B.E. in Textile Technology, or a fashion technology degree

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, ERP systems, fabric testing reports

items.label: Common starting titles
items.value: Sourcing executive, sourcing trainee, fabric coordinator

items.label: Direct employment in the textile sector
items.note: Figures differ by source and by whether informal work is counted
items.source: PIB / Ministry of Textiles statements (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Export houses and buying offices hire textile graduates as sourcing trainees, often through campus placement. Knowledge of fibres, yarns, weaves and fabric testing helps a textile graduate stand out from non-technical candidates.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Order tracking in Excel or ERP

value.title: At a glance
items: Work runs to buyer deadlines and seasonal calendars.
Common next steps: senior sourcing executive, sourcing manager, or merchandising.
Travel to mills and textile clusters is common.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
